neutro:
Use case: illustration-story. Create ONE finished neutral/base PROTAGONIST card portrait for the same dark, humble medieval fantasy game as the references. Exact portrait 3:4 aspect ratio, ideally 1152 x 1536. No text anywhere.
REFERENCES: Image 1 is the existing young heir: use his facial identity, age, hair shape and base clothing as the identity/character reference. Image 2 (the wagon illustration) is ONLY the artistic style and print palette reference, not the subject or layout.
Character: the SAME young lord, early twenties, elongated slightly angular rustic face, straight narrow nose, small tired eyes, short side-parted dark hair, clean-shaven, no crown. Preserve the first reference's recognizable facial proportions and hairline while translating the simple placeholder into the rich woodcut style of image 2. A coarse muted moss-green mantle over a simple brown tunic, plain worn leather belt, dull iron sword sheathed at the hip, no shining armor. Three-quarter length framing, head to upper thigh, centered and facing viewer, shoulders square but relaxed. Neutral expression: hesitant, responsible, a little tired; neither benevolent nor cruel. Hands resting naturally near his belt, not gripping the weapon. Modest everyday mantle, neither spotless nor heavily stained. No bread, no symbolic prop in this neutral base.
Style: fifteenth-century medieval woodcut / illuminated-manuscript illustration, lightly modernized; thick irregular black hand-carved contours, crosshatched shadows, rustic slightly stylized anatomy, flat printed pigments and slight registration offset. Match image 2's line weight, aged paper texture and color proportions closely. Restricted colors: ink black, earth brown, burnt ochre, rusty red, muted moss green. Parchment approximately #f3e6d3, fibrous aged paper. No smooth gradients, no cinematic shading.
Composition: solitary central person, no scene or other characters, generous plain parchment breathing room. Single thin simple black rectangular card border, inset slightly, not an ornamental arch. Head and torso placement must be suitable for creating two very closely matched variants later: clearly visible face, same viewpoint and scale. Keep the figure entire within the border.
Avoid: idealized handsome prince, glossy skin, anime eyes, gold glow, particles, dramatic heroic lighting, threatening villain lighting, 3D, polished armor, decorative frames, castle scenery, text, lettering, numerals, symbols containing writing, watermark. This is a poor, muddy, human world.

Keep head position, face angle, eye line, figure scale, overall silhouette and framing the same. Keep the SAME moss-green mantle, rusty-brown tunic, plain leather belt and dull sheathed iron sword, same garment construction, collar, seams and closures. Keep the same woodcut crosshatching, thick irregular carved ink line, flat earthy pigments, aged parchment fibers and thin black rectangular border. No letters, no numbers, no text.
ONLY SMALL LOCAL CHANGES: straighten the shoulders slightly for quiet resolve, clean the mantle of dirt while preserving rough coarse fabric, bend one forearm only enough to hold a SMALL plain loaf near the waist. The bread must remain a discreet secondary detail. The other hand rests naturally. Keep the neutral, tired, human expression; do not alter the facial anatomy or beautify him.
No smile of a saint, no heroic light, no halo, no gold, no particle effects, no glossy cloth, no new armor, no background scene. This is the same poor young lord in a slightly better state, not another character or costume. Preserve the original image as closely as possible outside the shoulders, mantle dirt and loaf-holding hand.
